item.title: Gram-positive and Gram-negative envelopes differ structurally
item.content: Gram-positive bacteria typically have a thick peptidoglycan layer and no Gram-negative-type outer membrane; Gram-negative bacteria have a thinner peptidoglycan layer plus an outer membrane containing lipopolysaccharide.
item.explanationMarkdown:
These envelope differences influence staining behavior and interactions with the environment.

The distinction is more informative than simply saying one group has “more wall.” Gram-negative cells possess an additional outer membrane, with the peptidoglycan located in the periplasmic region between the inner and outer membranes.

cards.front: What is the key envelope difference between typical Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria?
cards.back: Gram-positive: thick peptidoglycan, no Gram-negative outer membrane. Gram-negative: thin peptidoglycan plus an outer membrane containing LPS.
